title: Linear Regression, L1 vs L2 and Transformer Tensors
subject: #1: Linear Regression, L1 vs L2 and Transformer Tensors

questions.text: What is the closed-form solution of linear regression, and when do you use gradient descent instead?
questions.hint: Mention the normal equation and its cubic time complexity with respect to features. Contrast this with gradient descent for massive datasets.

questions.text: What are the differences between L1 and L2 regularization in logistic regression?
questions.hint: Explain sparsity via absolute penalties versus shrinkage via squared penalties, and how they behave with correlated features.

questions.text: A network confuses pugs and pit bulls and some training labels are wrong. How do you modify the model and the data?
questions.hint: Address noisy labels using robust loss functions or confidence weighting, and handle fine-grained visual classes using attention maps or metric learning.

questions.text: You need one embedding space for your own domain: product photos, spec sheets as PDFs, and text queries. Off-the-shelf CLIP is not good enough. How do you build it?
questions.hint: Discuss multi-modal joint embedding spaces, PDF parsing strategies, contrastive fine-tuning, and hard negative mining.

questions.text: GLM-4.5 is an MoE with 355B total but 32B active parameters. Explain the economics: what does that split buy you and what does it cost?
questions.hint: Analyze inference capacity scaling, memory bandwidth bottlenecks, routing overhead, and pre-training throughput tradeoffs.

questions.text: Walk me through what happens, tensor by tensor, in one forward pass of a decoder-only transformer.
questions.hint: Trace tokenization, embedding lookup, multi-head attention projections, residual additions, layer normalization, and feed-forward transformations.

questions.text: Your DPO run improved general chat evaluations but regressed math performance. What are your hypotheses for why this happened?
questions.hint: Explore reward hacking, catastrophic forgetting, and distribution shifts between conversational style data and precise reasoning benchmarks.

questions.text: How would you benchmark an LLM agent's tool use, say, for enterprise workflows composing 10+ APIs?
questions.hint: Propose multi-turn execution environments, deterministic mock APIs, correctness verification, and cost-latency profiling frameworks.

questions.text: Users ask “how many open orders are blocked on a supplier issue?” Plain RAG gets this wrong. Why, and what's the right architecture?
questions.hint: Highlight aggregation limitations of unstructured search, and advocate for Text-to-SQL or hybrid structured-unstructured retrieval pipelines.

questions.text: The patient's chart already lists their medications. How would you use that to improve transcription of drug names, and how would you keep it from backfiring?
questions.hint: Cover biasing speech recognition decoding graphs with patient vocabularies, alongside mitigation for hallucinations when charts are incomplete.

questions.text: How do you load test an LLM service so the numbers actually mean something?
questions.hint: Focus on realistic workload traffic patterns, TTFT versus ITL metrics, concurrency ramps, and avoiding synthetic client-side bottlenecks.

questions.text: When should you choose fine-tuning over RAG over prompt engineering?
questions.hint: Weigh cost, latency, update frequency, domain knowledge requirements, and security constraints across architectural choices.

questions.text: Why might replacing a dense feed-forward layer with a top-2 Mixture of Experts (MoE) increase end-to-end inference latency despite executing fewer FLOPs per token?
questions.hint: Mention memory bandwidth limits, non-contiguous expert memory accesses, dynamic batching fragmentation, and all-to-all communication overhead.

questions.text: What are Type I and Type II errors?
questions.hint: Define false positives and false negatives clearly in the context of hypothesis testing or classification thresholds.

questions.text: Implement beam search for an autoregressive model. When would an answer engine actually use it?
questions.hint: Describe probability tracking, pruning, and length penalties. Explain its use in high-stakes structured generation tasks.

deep_dive.text: Walk me through what happens, tensor by tensor, in one forward pass of a decoder-only transformer.
deep_dive.answer:
We begin with an input token sequence of shape (batch_size, sequence_length), which passes through an embedding layer to yield tensor X of shape (batch_size, seq_len, d_model).

Next, X enters the transformer block layers. Each layer applies RMSNorm or LayerNorm, followed by self-attention projections. We compute Query, Key, and Value tensors by multiplying X with weight matrices, reshaping to multi-head format (batch, heads, seq_len, d_head), applying causal masking, and computing scaled dot-product attention.

The attention output tensor is projected back to d_model, added to the original X via a residual connection, and normalized again. This tensor then passes through the feed-forward network, typically utilizing gated activations like SwiGLU, expanding hidden dimensions before projecting back to d_model.

After passing through all stacked decoder layers, the final tensor is normalized and projected via the language model head weight matrix to produce logits of shape (batch_size, seq_len, vocab_size), predicting the next token probabilities.
